contexts.text: Because he had as the end the pre-eminence of self before others...
The second origin of the falsities of doctrine is from... the desire of being pre-eminent. Signified.
In heavenly joy there is nothing of preeminence before another; and in proportion as there is pre-eminence, in the same proportion there is Hell.
Say they have laboured in the vineyard, when yet they have constantly revolved in mind the preeminence of self, honours, etc.
A man is not saved on account of his temptations, if he... thinks of his own pre-eminence before others... which is contrary to mutual love, and therefore to heavenly blessedness.

Those in knowledge... and not in the life of charity, cannot know of the existence of any delight except what results from pre-eminence; (whereas) heavenly delight results from humiliation, and the affection of being of service to others. Illustrated.
Merit regards man, and thus conjoins itself with... the thought of the pre-eminence of self over others, and consequently with contempt for others.
